classification.difficultyReason: Combine the two durations and distances and use total distance divided by total time for the whole-trip speed, rather than averaging the leg speeds; earlier parts scaffold the totals.

content.prompt: Henry travels $50\text{ km}$ by train in $\frac{3}{4}$ of an hour, and then cycles for $10\text{ km}$ in $\frac{4}{5}$ of an hour.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How long, in hours and minutes, did his whole trip take?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total time}&=\frac{3}{4}+\frac{4}{5}\\\text{Total time}&=\frac{15}{20}+\frac{16}{20}\\\text{Total time}&=1\frac{11}{20}\text{ h}\end{align*}$$
$$\frac{11}{20}\times60=33\text{ min}$$
The whole trip took 1 hour 33 minutes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is his average speed, in km/h, during the train trip?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Average train speed}&=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\\\text{Average train speed}&=50\div\frac{3}{4}\\\text{Average train speed}&=50\times\frac{4}{3}\\\text{Average train speed}&=66\frac{2}{3}\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is his average speed, in km/h, during the bike trip?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Average bike speed}&=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}\\\text{Average bike speed}&=10\div\frac{4}{5}\\\text{Average bike speed}&=10\times\frac{5}{4}\\\text{Average bike speed}&=12\frac{1}{2}\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What is his average speed over the whole trip?

answer.short:
$38\frac{22}{31}\text{ km/h}$

Divide the total distance by the total time.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total distance}&=50+10\\\text{Total distance}&=60\text{ km}\end{align*}$$
The total time is $\frac{31}{20}\text{ h}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average speed}&=\frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}\\\text{Average speed}&=60\div\frac{31}{20}\\\text{Average speed}&=\frac{1200}{31}\\\text{Average speed}&=38\frac{22}{31}\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$$
